question_text: Module 10 asks us to settle two things before beginning. According to the introduction, what are they?
answer_options: That every question has one neat answer, and that battles end at salvation
That following Jesus does not mean you stop having questions, and that the new life comes with a real battle
That questions show weak faith, and that hardship is God's punishment
That wisdom comes only through leaders, and that the battle is fought for us
correct_answer: That following Jesus does not mean you stop having questions, and that the new life comes with a real battle

question_text: The module says that if life has felt harder since you believed, that is not a sign you did something wrong. What does it say this is a sign of?
answer_options: That you have not yet prayed enough for protection
That your faith is still too small to bring peace
That God is testing whether you deserve His blessings
That you switched sides, and your God has already won
correct_answer: That you switched sides, and your God has already won

question_text: On why bad things happen to good people, the module gently challenges the question itself using Romans 3:23. What does it say is the real wonder?
answer_options: Not that hard things happen to good people, but that God is so good to people like us
That good people suffer more than bad people in this life
That God allows any suffering at all in the world He made
That suffering always ends once a person turns to Christ
correct_answer: Not that hard things happen to good people, but that God is so good to people like us

question_text: The module lists the sources suffering can come from. Which option matches the list given under 'Where Does Suffering Come From?'
answer_options: Weak faith, unconfessed sin, poor choices, and bad company
Fate, chance, generational curses, and divine anger
A broken world, other people's choices, your own choices, and a real enemy
God's discipline, natural law, human error, and coincidence
correct_answer: A broken world, other people's choices, your own choices, and a real enemy

question_text: Referring to the man born blind in John 9:3, what point does the module make about suffering?
answer_options: Suffering is not always punishment — the man's blindness was not from sin, but so God's works could be shown
Suffering is always traceable to someone's hidden sin
Physical healing depends on first confessing every sin
God sends blindness so that people will learn humility
correct_answer: Suffering is not always punishment — the man's blindness was not from sin, but so God's works could be shown

question_text: The module illustrates God's role in pain with a doctor setting a broken bone. What is this illustration teaching?
answer_options: Pain proves that God has stepped away until the healing is complete
God causes evil so that He can later display His power in healing it
Believers should avoid asking why and simply endure whatever comes
God is never the author of evil, but He works toward healing and purpose you cannot yet see
correct_answer: God is never the author of evil, but He works toward healing and purpose you cannot yet see

question_text: On betting and Christianity, the module says the real issue is not the money. According to the teaching, what is the real issue?
answer_options: The amount wagered — small stakes are harmless, large stakes are sinful
Your heart — where your trust is and where your treasure is
The legality of gambling in your country of residence
Whether the winnings are given generously to the church
correct_answer: Your heart — where your trust is and where your treasure is

question_text: Under 'Faith vs. Fortune', the module names a devastating spiritual effect of gambling. What is it?
answer_options: It wastes time that should be spent in church activities
It makes a person too wealthy to depend on God's provision
It weakens a person's faith by shifting their focus from God as their source to luck
It causes conflict with fellow believers over borrowed money
correct_answer: It weakens a person's faith by shifting their focus from God as their source to luck

question_text: How does the module describe water baptism and its relationship to salvation?
answer_options: It is the moment a believer is actually saved and born again
It is optional and carries no particular significance for a believer
It washes away only the sins committed before the baptism date
It is the outward declaration that you have died to the old life and risen new in Christ — it does not save you, but it is a step of obedience Jesus asked for
correct_answer: It is the outward declaration that you have died to the old life and risen new in Christ — it does not save you, but it is a step of obedience Jesus asked for

question_text: 'Why Is It Suddenly Hard?' closes with four 'Note This' points about hardships. Which option states all four as taught?
answer_options: Hardships are a reality in salvation; they test our faith; when endured we become mature and complete; and they produce everlasting glory
Hardships come from the enemy alone; they must be rebuked; they end quickly for the faithful; and they leave no lasting benefit
Hardships mean hidden sin; they call for fasting; they are removed by giving; and they return if faith weakens
Hardships are rare after salvation; they signal wrong choices; they are avoided by wisdom; and they fade with maturity
correct_answer: Hardships are a reality in salvation; they test our faith; when endured we become mature and complete; and they produce everlasting glory
